## 3. The proposed \(x=.414\) input is strictly negative, with overflow paid

I subjected the supplied `.414` candidate to a stronger exact interval calculation. This was necessary because its apparent coherent information was close enough to zero that ordinary numerical signs were unreliable.

The actual tested input has:

- Fock support \(0,\ldots,159\);
- explicitly recorded integer amplitudes and rational mixing probability;
- a two-dimensional purification reference;
- receiver cutoff \(J=261\), with an unconditional overflow flag;
- no truncation of the true complementary environment.

Long-double eigenvectors only propose spectra. Acceptance uses exact integer/rational matrix intervals, residual bounds and entropy enclosures.

For the cutoff channel, the certified coherent-information interval is
\[
\begin{aligned}
I_c\in[
&-0.000000000000109605253957852739,\\
&-0.000000000000108576051015232132
].
\end{aligned}
\]

The receiver overflow obeys
\[
q\le 4.2112684195527\times10^{-22}.
\]
For a fixed input with purification dimension \(d_R\), I used
\[
0\le I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-I_c(\rho,C_J\mathcal N)
\le 2h_2(q)+2q\log_2d_R.
\]
The first term pays the receiver-sector pinching; the second pays the information discarded inside the overflow sector. The overflow flag remains available. No successful branch is postselected.

Here the correction is at most \(6.18643\times10^{-20}\) bits. Consequently the **actual uncut channel** still has
\[
I_c\in
[-1.09605254\times10^{-13},
 -1.08575989\times10^{-13}]
\]
with the displayed endpoints rounded outwards.

This rejects **that specific input at `.414`**. It does not establish zero capacity at `.414`, exclude other inputs, or exclude longer codes.

The energy contract is also explicit: every state in the two-vector input span, including arbitrary reference-entangled inputs, has mean photon number at most \(60.243183\). The hard cutoff gives the coarser uniform bound \(159\). These are real finite-energy bounds, but the tested input does not have positive coherent information.
